questions.question: What is the primary purpose of APA style according to the chapter?

answers.text: To make psychological writing sound more scientific and technical
To facilitate scientific communication by promoting clarity and standardizing organization
To ensure all psychology papers are written in a formal literary style
To replace MLA style as the universal academic writing standard

questions.question: According to the chapter, which of the following is NOT a standard section of an APA-style empirical research report?

answers.text: Abstract
Literature Review
Method
Discussion

questions.question: What does the chapter identify as the 'second level' of APA style?

answers.text: Low-level style including grammar and spelling rules
High-level style including formal and straightforward writing
The organization of research articles into sections
Reference formatting and citation rules

questions.question: According to the chapter, why should researchers avoid using direct quotations frequently in APA-style writing?

answers.text: Direct quotations are too difficult to format correctly
Psychological phenomena and theories are objective and do not depend on specific words used
Direct quotations make the reference list too long
Other researchers prefer paraphrasing over direct quotes

questions.question: When citing a work with three to five authors for the first time in APA style, what should you do?

answers.text: Include only the first author's name followed by et al.
Include all authors' names
Include only the first two authors' names
Include all authors' names followed by et al.

questions.question: What term should be used instead of 'sexual preference' according to APA guidelines discussed in the chapter?

answers.text: Sexual identity
Sexual orientation
Sexual lifestyle
Sexual tendency

questions.question: According to Daryl Bem's recommendations in the chapter, how should a research report introduction begin?

answers.text: With a detailed literature review of previous studies
With general observations about the topic in ordinary language about people and behavior
With a formal statement of the research hypothesis
With technical jargon to establish credibility

questions.question: What is the recommended maximum length for an APA-style article title?

answers.text: 8 words or fewer
12 words or fewer
15 words or fewer
20 words or fewer

questions.question: In an APA-style reference for a journal article, which elements are italicized?

answers.text: The article title and journal title
The journal title and volume number
The journal title and issue number
Only the journal title

questions.question: According to the chapter, what should the abstract of an APA-style research report typically be limited to?

answers.text: About 100 words
About 200 words
About 300 words
About 500 words

questions.question: Which principle for avoiding biased language involves referring to 'people diagnosed with schizophrenia' rather than 'schizophrenics'?

answers.text: Using more specific terms
Putting the person first
Avoiding objectifying participants
Being sensitive to labels

questions.question: What does the chapter recommend regarding the use of 'et al.' after the first citation of a work?

answers.text: Never use et al. for works with fewer than six authors
Use et al. after the first citation for works with three to five authors
Always spell out all authors' names regardless of citation number
Use et al. only in parenthetical citations

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is the purpose of the literature review in an introduction?

answers.text: To list all previous studies on the topic chronologically
To construct an argument for why the research question is worth addressing
To demonstrate the researcher's knowledge of the field
To criticize previous researchers' methodologies

questions.question: In the method section, what principle should guide the level of detail included?

answers.text: Include every detail so the manuscript appears thorough
Include enough detail that other researchers could replicate the study
Keep it brief to maintain reader interest
Focus only on novel aspects of the methodology

questions.question: According to the chapter, what should typically be discussed first in the results section?

answers.text: The most surprising findings
Preliminary issues such as data exclusions and variable computation
The main hypothesis test
Secondary analyses

questions.question: What structure does Bem (2003) suggest for discussing each new result in the results section?

answers.text: Present statistics first, then explain in words
Remind readers of the question, answer in words, present statistics, qualify if necessary, and summarize
State the hypothesis, present statistics, and move to the next result
Describe the statistical test, report the results, and interpret the findings

questions.question: According to the chapter, what typically comes immediately after the participants subsection in a simple method section organization?

answers.text: Materials subsection
Design and procedure subsection
Separate design subsection
Apparatus subsection

questions.question: What does the chapter say about discussing limitations in the discussion section?

answers.text: List every possible limitation to show thoroughness
Avoid mentioning limitations as they weaken the study
Pick two or three limitations that could have influenced results and explain how
Only mention limitations if reviewers specifically ask

questions.question: For poster presentations at conferences, what font size does the chapter recommend for the title and authors' names?

answers.text: 28 points
48 points
72 points
96 points

questions.question: According to the chapter, how should information on a poster be organized for optimal readability?

answers.text: In rows that flow across the poster from left to right
In columns that flow from top to bottom
In a circular pattern starting from the center
In a single large block of text
